Why would a children's heart surgeon ask Ferrari for help?
At Great Ormond Street Hospital in London, a baby has just survived heart surgery.
Next: the move from surgery to intensive care.
Every tube, wire and monitor gets unplugged, moved, and plugged back in.
Several teams crowd one tiny bed, and small details slip through.
Then two of its doctors watched a Formula One pit stop and saw the same problem, solved.
Twenty mechanics. One car. Four new tyres in seconds, and nobody gets in anyone's way.
Ferrari's crew studied videos of the hospital's handovers and picked them apart.
The fix came straight from the pit lane.
One leader runs the handover, just like the lollipop man.
Everyone gets one job, done in a fixed order.
And a checklist makes sure nothing gets forgotten.
The result? Technical errors dropped by forty-two percent, and missing information was almost cut in half.
A sport obsessed with saving tenths of a second taught doctors to protect their smallest patients.
So next time someone asks you...
